claim.quote: we reach a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV, in agreement with the standard model prediction.

date.note: arXiv submission date; CMS announced the measurement on 17 September 2024 and it was published as Nature 652 (2026) 321

key_value.quote: a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV

name: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the W boson more precisely than any other LHC experiment, and found it to agree with the standard model - unlike an earlier, conflicting result from the Tevatron.
summary.technical: W -> mu nu events from 2016 13 TeV data, high-granularity maximum likelihood fit to muon kinematics with in situ constraints on theory inputs: m_W = 80 360.2 +/- 9.9 MeV.

title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment
why_it_matters: The W and Z masses are related in the standard model, so a precise W mass is a sensitive probe of undiscovered heavy particles entering through quantum loops.
